 Vehicle Recalls Flag Steering, Wheel and Fire Risks
 Free Press Publisher 
 October 26, 2026 
 Lifestyle and Travel News , Notices 
 The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has listed 10 recalls involving vehicles with potential wheel, steering, fuel system, battery, camera and instrument display problems. Two include “Do Not Drive” notices.
 The recalls cover certain vehicles in the following model years:
 Porsche, recall 26V682: A center lock may break and cause a wheel to detach. The “Do Not Drive” notice covers certain 2024 718 Cayman GT4 RS, 718 Spyder RS, 911, 911 Carrera GTS, 911 GT3, 911 GT3 RS, 911 Turbo and 911 Turbo S vehicles.
 Subaru, recall 26V685: A “Do Not Drive” notice involving potential loss of vehicle control covers certain 2026 Crosstrek and Forester vehicles.
 Ford, recall 26V653: Inaccurate speedometer and tachometer displays affect certain 2026 F-150 and F-750 SD trucks, along with 2025–2026 F-250 SD, F-350 SD, F-450 SD, F-550 SD and F-600 SD trucks.
 Toyota, recall 26V673: Fuel tubes may disconnect and leak in certain 2024–2027 Land Cruiser Hybrid vehicles.
 Volvo Trucks, recall 26V677: Certain 2025–2026 VNL (4) trucks may have loose or missing structural bolts in the cab.
 Land Rover, recall 26V678: Water may damage the rearview camera in certain 2022–2026 Range Rover vehicles.
 Lexus, recall 26V687: Instrument panel display failure affects certain 2022–2024 NX, NX Hybrid and NX Plug-in Hybrid vehicles.
 Hyundai, recall 26V692: Loose fasteners may cause loss of steering control in certain 2026 Elantra and Tucson Hybrid vehicles.
 Hyundai, recall 26V693: A wheel may detach from certain 2026 Elantra, Elantra Hybrid, Elantra N and Venue vehicles.
 Audi, recall 26V698: The high-voltage battery may catch fire in certain 2024–2025 Q4 e-tron and Q4 Sportback e-tron vehicles.
 Owners can enter their license plate or vehicle identification number in NHTSA’s Recall Lookup Tool to determine whether their vehicle has an unrepaired recall. Recall repairs are free through dealerships. Owners of vehicles covered by the Porsche and Subaru “Do Not Drive” notices should not drive the affected vehicles.

 The Franklin County Free Press, established by Vicky Taylor in 2019, emerged as a beacon of local journalism for the residents of Franklin County. Under Vicky's leadership, it quickly became an essential source of news, particularly at a time when major newspaper publications were increasingly overlooking local coverage. 
On January 1, 2022, the torch was passed to Nathan Neil and his firm, Neil Publishing, LLC. Neil, a local entrepreneur with multiple thriving businesses in Chambersburg, shares Vicky's fervent commitment to both the community and the world of local journalism. 
Rooted in the heart of Franklin County and powered by its residents, the Franklin County Free Press continues to bridge the gap, ensuring that the local stories, events, and issues that matter most to the community remain in the spotlight.
